summary: **Decision:** Configure Prettier as explicit default formatter in VSCode settings to prevent Biome extension from mass-reformatting files. **Problem:** With formatOnSave enabled and no explicit formatter specified, Biome extension overrode Prettier, causing 4,636 files to be reformatted (tabs instead of spaces, double quotes instead of single). **Alternatives:** Disable formatOnSave (rejected: loses convenience); uninstall Biome (rejected: may be needed); add to .gitignore (rejected: doesn't prevent). **Trade-offs:** Explicit per-language formatter config adds verbosity but ensures consistency. **Impact/Scope:** All developers using VSCode/Cursor on this repo. **Pattern:** Always specify explicit formatter in .vscode/settings.json for TS/JS/JSON files when multiple formatters may be installed.

**Decision:** Implement Payload CMS Pages collection with blocks-based content model for multi-tenant landing page builder. **Problem:** Need flexible, structured way to define page layouts with different section types (hero, text, CTA, features) while supporting multiple design systems and multi-tenancy. **Implementation:** Created Pages collection with tenantId/userId indexing, strict slug validation (lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens), designSystem selector (untitledui/shadcn), and sections field using Payload blocks API with 4 block types. Added Media collection for image uploads. **Alternatives:** Hardcoded sections array (rejected: inflexible); free-form JSON (rejected: no validation); page templates (rejected: less flexible). **Trade-offs:** Blocks provide structure and validation but require more upfront schema definition. **Impact/Scope:** Foundation for TASK-011 (templates), TASK-012 (auth), TASK-013 (API). **Pattern:** Use Payload blocks for structured, repeatable content sections; validate slugs with regex; index multi-tenant fields; use select fields for design system variants.

**Decision:** Implement multi-tenant access control using official @payloadcms/plugin-multi-tenant package instead of manual implementation. **Problem:** Need to enforce tenant isolation so users can only access their own tenant's pages while admins can access all tenants. **Implementation:** Configured plugin to automatically inject 'tenant' relationship field (removed manual tenantId text field), created Users collection with roles (admin/user), created Tenants collection, implemented userHasAccessToAllTenants function to bypass filtering for admin role. Access control at collection level: read/create/update/delete hooks check user role and tenant assignment. **Alternatives:** Manual tenant filtering in each query (rejected: error-prone, no admin UI); middleware-based filtering (rejected: not Payload best practice); custom plugin (rejected: maintenance burden). **Trade-offs:** Plugin dependency adds complexity but provides tested solution with admin UI integration. Plugin auto-injects fields which required test updates. TypeScript types incomplete in v3.65.0 requiring justified @ts-expect-error. **Impact/Scope:** All Payload collections (Pages, Users, Tenants). 73 tests passing (42 access control, 31 schema). Fixed 3 pre-existing TypeScript errors. **Pattern:** Use official plugins for cross-cutting concerns; place access control in collection definitions; admin bypass via role checking; flexible tenant extraction for different data formats.

**Decision:** Use type guard pattern with .filter(hasName) when accessing Payload CMS Field properties in tests. **Problem:** Payload's Field type is a union including UIField and RowField which don't have 'name', 'required', 'unique', 'validate', 'options', 'hasMany', 'defaultValue', 'minRows', 'blocks', 'fields', or 'relationTo' properties, causing TypeScript errors. **Alternatives:** Use 'as any' casts (rejected: loses type safety); ignore errors with @ts-expect-error (rejected: masks real issues). **Trade-offs:** Slightly more verbose test code but maintains type safety and provides clear intent. **Impact/Scope:** All Payload CMS test files that inspect collection field schemas. **Pattern:** Create hasName type guard: `const hasName = (field: Field): field is Field & { name: string } => 'name' in field`. Use `.filter(hasName)` before `.find()` or `.map()` on field arrays. Add type assertions for accessed properties: `as (Field & { required?: boolean; unique?: boolean }) | undefined`.

**Decision:** Remove all Builder.io code and dependencies after Payload CMS migration is complete. **Problem:** Builder.io was a third-party headless CMS dependency that added complexity, API key management overhead, and limited control over page rendering. **Alternatives:** Keep Builder.io alongside Payload (rejected: maintenance burden, confusing dual systems); gradual migration (rejected: technical debt accumulation). **Trade-offs:** Breaking change requiring removal of preview routes that depended on Builder.io; gained full control over content management and reduced external dependencies. **Impact/Scope:** Removed @builder.io/sdk-react-nextjs and @builder.io/sdk packages; deleted src/libs/builder/, src/app/builder-preview/, src/app/(backend)/api/builder/, src/server/services/builder/, tests/e2e/builder/, and Builder artifact type from ArtifactType enum. **Pattern:** When migrating away from a third-party CMS: (1) implement replacement first, (2) verify it works, (3) remove all old code including types, env vars, and test files, (4) run full build/test suite before declaring complete.

**Decision:** Payload CMS v3 admin panel requires Next.js integration - standalone Express server does not serve admin UI. **Problem:** apps/payload uses Express-only server (src/server.ts) which initializes Payload but returns 404 for /admin routes. Payload v3 changed to use Next.js for admin panel rendering. **Alternatives:** Keep Express-only (rejected: no admin UI); migrate to @payloadcms/next (recommended for admin access); use Local API only (current: tests work, no visual admin). **Trade-offs:** Current setup works for Local API and testing (105 tests pass) but no admin UI access. To get admin panel, need to either integrate with main Next.js app or add @payloadcms/next package. **Impact/Scope:** apps/payload server setup; future admin panel access; Phase 3 API integration may need adjustment. **Pattern:** For Payload v3, use Next.js integration (@payloadcms/next) for admin UI; Express standalone only supports Local API and REST endpoints, not admin panel.

**Decision:** Payload v3 Next.js admin requires three critical props: importMap, serverFunction, and config in both layout.tsx and page.tsx files. **Problem:** Admin panel returning 500 errors with 'Cannot read properties of undefined' for RSC components like TenantSelectionProvider. Plugin components registered in importMap.js but not being resolved. **Root Cause:** layout.tsx was missing importMap and serverFunction props. page.tsx was missing importMap prop. **Solution:** (1) In layout.tsx: import handleServerFunctions from @payloadcms/next/layouts, create serverFunction using 'use server' directive that calls handleServerFunctions({...args, config, importMap}), pass importMap and serverFunction to RootLayout. (2) In page.tsx: import importMap from '../importMap' and pass to RootPage({config, importMap, params, searchParams}). **Monorepo Issues:** turbopack.root and outputFileTracingRoot must both be set to monorepo root for pnpm hoisted node_modules. TypeScript imports should not use .js extensions. **Impact/Scope:** All Payload v3 Next.js projects using plugins with RSC components. **Pattern:** Always pass importMap and serverFunction to RootLayout, importMap to RootPage. Check plugin docs for RSC component requirements.

**Decision:** Seed default tenant via direct SQL before first user creation when using @payloadcms/plugin-multi-tenant. **Problem:** Chicken-and-egg bootstrap issue - create-first-user form requires selecting a tenant from Tenants collection, but no tenants exist and API requires authentication to create tenants. Form shows 'This field is required' error on Tenants dropdown with empty options, returning 400 Bad Request on /api/users/first-register. **Solution:** Insert seed tenant directly into database before first user creation: `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "INSERT INTO tenants (name, slug, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('Default Tenant', 'default', NOW(), NOW());"`. **Alternatives:** Modify plugin to make tenant optional for first user (rejected: requires plugin fork); disable multi-tenant for first user only (rejected: complex conditional logic); pre-seeded database (chosen: simplest, one-time operation). **Trade-offs:** Requires database access for initial setup; not fully automated. **Impact/Scope:** Any Payload CMS project using @payloadcms/plugin-multi-tenant with fresh database. **Pattern:** For multi-tenant Payload projects, document this bootstrap requirement in setup instructions. Consider adding seed migration or setup script.

**Decision:** Payload CMS and LobeChat MUST use separate databases or proper table isolation to prevent table naming conflicts. **Problem:** Payload CMS migration (Nov 30, 2025) created users, tenants, media tables without prefixes, overwriting/conflicting with LobeChat Drizzle tables. After Payload migration ran, all LobeChat tables (sessions, ai_models, user_settings, chat_groups, ai_providers, agents, messages, etc.) were missing, breaking the app with 'relation does not exist' errors. **Alternatives:** (1) Separate databases (recommended), (2) Use Payload schema/table prefix config, (3) Manual table renaming (fragile). **Trade-offs:** Separate databases add operational complexity but guarantee isolation. **Impact/Scope:** Any shared PostgreSQL database between Payload CMS and LobeChat; affects all database queries after auth. **Pattern:** Never share a single database between Payload CMS and LobeChat without verified table isolation. Always check for table name conflicts before running migrations from different ORMs (Drizzle vs Payload) on the same database.

**Decision:** Adding a new Settings tab requires updates in THREE locations, not just the component map. **Problem:** Tenant settings UI was implemented but invisible - the tab didn't appear in the sidebar because the menu item wasn't added. **Alternatives:** Single source of truth config (rejected: requires larger refactor of existing pattern). **Trade-offs:** Accept current 3-location pattern; document clearly. **Impact/Scope:** All future settings tab additions (SettingsTabs enum, SettingsContent componentMap, useCategory sidebar menu). **Pattern:** For new settings tabs: 1) Add to SettingsTabs enum in src/store/global/initialState.ts, 2) Add dynamic import to componentMap in src/app/[variants]/(main)/settings/_layout/SettingsContent.tsx, 3) Add menu item with icon to useCategory hook in src/app/[variants]/(main)/settings/hooks/useCategory.tsx, 4) Add translation key to src/locales/default/setting.ts tab section.

**Decision:** TenantRepository accesses Payload CMS via REST API, not direct database queries. **Problem:** Main app runs on port 3010, Payload CMS on port 3011 - relative API calls fail, and shared database access would couple the systems. **Alternatives:** Direct Payload database query (rejected: tight coupling, schema drift risk); GraphQL (rejected: Payload uses REST). **Trade-offs:** HTTP overhead accepted for clean separation; requires PAYLOAD_API_URL env var. **Impact/Scope:** All tenant-related operations in main app (domain automation, tenant settings). **Pattern:** For cross-service data access: 1) Create env config for external service URL, 2) Implement repository with REST calls, 3) Expose via tRPC for frontend use.

**Decision:** React components with multiple conditional UI states must explicitly handle null/undefined edge cases, not just expected enum values. **Problem:** DomainSettings component only handled three domainStatus states (null domain, pending_verification, verified) but actual data had domain='ceremoniacircle.org' with domainStatus=null (legacy data), causing nothing to render. **Alternatives:** Default to first matching state (rejected: hides data issues); throw error (rejected: poor UX). **Trade-offs:** Extra conditional block adds complexity but prevents silent rendering failures. **Impact/Scope:** All UI components with enum-based conditional rendering, especially settings/config pages that may have legacy data. **Pattern:** For enum-driven conditional UI: 1) List ALL possible state combinations including null/undefined, 2) Add explicit 'fallback' or 'needs-attention' state for unexpected combinations, 3) Add data-status attributes for E2E testing each state.

**Decision:** Edge middleware must not import Node.js-only modules (pino, database) - use dynamic imports for auth/db code paths. **Problem:** Vercel Edge runtime hangs indefinitely when middleware imports Node.js libraries like pino logger or database clients via @/auth. SSL handshake succeeds but server never responds. **Alternatives:** Force Node.js runtime for middleware (rejected: slower cold starts, defeats Edge benefits); remove tenant domain routing (rejected: core feature). **Trade-offs:** Dynamic imports add slight complexity but allow Edge-compatible middleware while preserving Node.js features for auth flows that need them. **Impact/Scope:** All middleware code in src/proxy.ts; any service imported by middleware. **Pattern:** For Edge middleware: (1) Never import pino/winston - use console.log, (2) Use dynamic import() for auth/database modules, (3) Keep tenant domain lookup as pure functions returning static data or simple HTTP fetches.

**Decision:** Use aggressive memory optimizations in next.config.ts to avoid Vercel OOM build failures on large codebases. **Problem:** Vercel Hobby plan provides 8GB build memory which is insufficient for lobe-builder's ~500+ page Next.js app with webpack. Build fails with SIGKILL/OOM during webpack compilation. **Alternatives:** Upgrade to Vercel Pro for 16GB (rejected: cost for this use case); use Docker self-hosted builds (rejected: operational complexity); optimize build config (chosen). **Trade-offs:** Build time increases from ~7min to ~13min, but build completes successfully. Disabled source maps reduce debugging capability in production. **Impact/Scope:** All Vercel deployments of lobe-builder; any large Next.js app hitting memory limits. **Pattern:** For OOM builds: (1) Set experimental.cpus: 1 to serialize workers, (2) Set serverSourceMaps: false, (3) Set productionBrowserSourceMaps: false. These settings in next.config.ts reduce peak memory at cost of build parallelism and debugging.

**Decision:** Vercel Deployment Protection must be disabled for public landing pages in multi-tenant applications. **Problem:** Deployment Protection returns 401 with SSO nonce cookie for all requests including unauthenticated landing pages at /page/* and /lp/* routes. The 'live.ceremoniacircle.org' custom domain returns 404 because middleware rewrites to protected internal routes. **Alternatives:** Use Vercel Pro for path-based bypass rules (requires paid plan); serve landing pages from separate unprotected project (rejected: defeats integration); implement app-level auth (rejected: landing pages must be public). **Trade-offs:** Disabling protection exposes all routes; must rely on app-level middleware for route-specific access control. **Impact/Scope:** All tenant landing pages; custom domain routing via middleware; any public content on protected Vercel projects. **Pattern:** For multi-tenant landing pages: (1) Disable Vercel Deployment Protection at project level, (2) Implement route-specific access control in Next.js middleware, (3) Use separate Vercel projects if mixed public/private content is needed.

**Decision:** Add all public landing page routes (/page/*, /preview/*, /lp/*) to Clerk's isPublicRoute matcher, not just the middleware bypass. **Problem:** Landing pages returned 404 despite middleware bypass because Clerk's auth.protect() runs BEFORE defaultMiddleware. The bypass in defaultMiddleware (NextResponse.next()) was never reached for protected routes. Headers showed x-clerk-auth-reason: dev-browser-missing and x-matched-path: /404. **Alternatives:** Disable Clerk entirely for landing domains (rejected: breaks other auth features); use separate deployment (rejected: operational complexity). **Trade-offs:** Routes listed in two places (matcher config and isPublicRoute) but ensures proper auth bypass order. **Impact/Scope:** All public-facing routes in multi-tenant apps using Clerk auth; custom domain landing pages. **Pattern:** For Clerk middleware: (1) Add route to config.matcher if not already there, (2) Add to isPublicRoute matcher BEFORE any auth checks, (3) The bypass in defaultMiddleware is for variant prefix, not auth.

**Decision:** When constructing URL rewrites in middleware, always verify slash placement between path segments. **Problem:** The /lp/{slug} rewrite produced malformed URLs like /page/ceremoniasoftening-the-season instead of /page/ceremonia/softening-the-season. Bug was in template literal: `/page/${tenantId}${slug}` missing slash before slug. **Alternatives:** N/A - straightforward bug fix. **Trade-offs:** None. **Impact/Scope:** All /lp/* routes on custom tenant domains were broken. **Pattern:** When using string templates for URL construction: (1) Verify each path segment has proper separators, (2) Test with actual slugs not just 'home', (3) Check URL rewrite logs show expected paths.

**Decision:** Domain automation requires four env vars: VERCEL_API_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, VERCEL_TEAM_ID (optional), and PAYLOAD_API_URL. **Problem:** Production tenant settings failed with 'VERCEL_API_TOKEN is required' error, and domain displayed wrong value (ceremoniacircle.org vs live.ceremoniacircle.org). **Alternatives:** N/A - env vars must be configured in Vercel dashboard. **Trade-offs:** Requires manual Vercel dashboard configuration; cannot be automated via code. **Impact/Scope:** All domain automation features (add, verify, remove domains); tenant settings UI; any deployment using VercelDomain module. **Pattern:** For multi-tenant domain automation: (1) Create Vercel API token at vercel.com/account/tokens, (2) Add VERCEL_API_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID to Vercel env vars, (3) Add PAYLOAD_API_URL pointing to Payload CMS, (4) Redeploy after adding env vars. Fix wrong domain values via Payload Admin UI or domain.remove + domain.add flow.

**Decision:** tRPC domain router permission check must use fields that actually exist in AuthContext. **Problem:** domain.remove endpoint returned UNAUTHORIZED despite user being authenticated. hasAdminPermission function checked for ctx.tenants array that was never populated in tRPC context creation. AuthContext only includes: userId, clerkAuth, oidcAuth, nextAuth - no tenants field. **Alternatives:** Add tenants to context via middleware (rejected: requires Payload API calls on every request, performance overhead); implement proper tenant-role checking (rejected: not needed for MVP). **Trade-offs:** MVP simplified permission model (all authenticated users are admins) reduces security granularity but acceptable for single-tenant-per-user scenarios. **Impact/Scope:** All domain management operations (add, verify, remove); future multi-tenant user management will need proper tenant-role checking via Payload CMS Users collection. **Pattern:** For tRPC permission checks: (1) Verify context fields exist in AuthContext interface, (2) Check middleware chain populates expected fields, (3) For MVP, use available fields (userId) instead of assuming complex structures, (4) Document MVP approach and future enhancement path.

**Decision:** Always handle both Web API Headers (.get() method) and Node.js plain object headers when accessing request headers in Payload CMS access control functions. **Problem:** Service-to-service auth via x-payload-service-secret header failed with 403 because hasServiceAuth used req.headers.get() which only works for Web API Headers, not plain object headers that Payload may provide. Additionally, Vercel env vars can have trailing newlines causing string comparisons to fail silently. **Alternatives:** Use only .get() (rejected: doesn't work for Node.js objects); use only property access (rejected: doesn't work for Web API Headers). **Trade-offs:** Slightly more verbose code to handle both cases, but ensures compatibility across runtime environments. **Impact/Scope:** All Payload CMS access control functions that read custom headers; all Vercel env vars used in string comparisons. **Pattern:** (1) Check typeof headers.get === 'function' before using .get(), otherwise use property access. (2) When adding Vercel env vars via CLI, use echo -n to prevent trailing newlines. (3) When debugging auth failures, verify env var values don't have hidden whitespace.

**Decision:** Always check Vercel environment variables for embedded literal '
' characters before using them in API calls or string comparisons. **Problem:** Vercel env vars added via CLI or dashboard can have literal '
' appended (e.g., 'prj_xxx
' instead of 'prj_xxx'). This session found VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, VERCEL_TEAM_ID, and PAYLOAD_SERVICE_SECRET all affected, causing: (1) API calls returning 403/404 due to malformed project/team IDs, (2) String comparisons failing silently for auth tokens. **Alternatives:** N/A - bug in how env vars were added originally. **Trade-offs:** Must delete and re-add env vars via Vercel API to fix. **Impact/Scope:** All Vercel env vars used in string matching or URL construction. **Pattern:** (1) When adding env vars via CLI, use 'echo -n value | vercel env add KEY production' to avoid newlines. (2) When debugging API failures, pull env vars and check with xxd/hexdump for hidden characters. (3) Consider trimming env vars at runtime: value.replace(/\n/g, '').trim().

**Decision:** When using react-i18next with placeholder variables like `{{domain}}`, pass interpolation values as an object, not a JavaScript template literal fallback. **Problem:** UI showed literal `{{domain}}` instead of the actual domain value because the component used `t('key', \`Domain: ${tenant.domain}\`)` which only sets the fallback string, not the interpolation values. **Alternatives:** N/A - straightforward bug fix. **Trade-offs:** Slightly more verbose code but ensures i18next interpolation works correctly. **Impact/Scope:** All react-i18next translations using variable placeholders. **Pattern:** Use `t('key', { defaultValue: 'Text with {{var}}', var: actualValue })` instead of `t('key', \`Text with ${actualValue}\`)`. The second argument must be an object with interpolation values, not a string.

**Decision:** Import from `@lobechat/utils/client` (not `@lobechat/utils`) for browser utilities like exportFile/exportJSONFile; use fallback pattern in ahooks callbacks. **Problem:** Direct import from `@lobechat/utils` fails with 'no exported member' errors; early-return pattern in useLocalStorageState callbacks causes undefined type errors. **Alternatives:** N/A - straightforward bug fixes. **Trade-offs:** None - correct import paths and type-safe patterns. **Impact/Scope:** All client-side code using @lobechat/utils exports; any ahooks useLocalStorageState usage with setData callbacks. **Pattern:** (1) Use `@lobechat/utils/client` for browser exports. (2) In useLocalStorageState callbacks, use `const current = prev || createDefault()` instead of `if (\!prev) return prev`.
